newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron resumes work on India's Dabhol Power.
newsitem.headline: Enron resumes work on India's Dabhol Power.

text.p: Enron Corp of the U.S. said on Tuesday financing of its Indian unit Dabhol Power Company has closed and it has resumed construction.

"We have been working toward this accomplishment for some time and we are extremely pleased that it has occured," a statement issued by Dabhol Power quoted Enron chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay as saying.
"Our goal now is focusing on completing construction. With nearly half of the 4,000 workers who will construct this plant on site immediately, we are well-positioned to meet this goal."

A commercial bank syndicate led by Bank of America and ABN-AMRO is providing $150 million of the funding, the Overseas Private Investment Corp (OPIC) $100 million and the U.S. Export-Import Bank $298 million based on a guarantee from a group of Indian financial institutions led by the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI).
IDBI is the lead arranger for a rupee loan provided by Indian financial institutions amounting to $98 million, the statement said.

The remainder of the project cost will be funded through owners' equity in the proportion of 80 percent Enron, 10 percent each by U.S. firms Bechtel Group Inc and General Electric Capital Services, it said.
The project's first phase will cost about $1.0 billion.

Last week, the Bombay high court dismissed a lawsuit against the Dabhol Power Company and, as a result of this ruling, all approvals and clearances granted to the project are legally binding, the company said.

Work has resumed on the first phase of construction of the 826 MW (gross) or 740 MW (exportable) combined cycle power plant in the western state Maharashtra which was embroiled in major controversies and over 20 court cases.
Dabhol Power intends to expand the project, ultimately bringing total plant size to 2,450 MW (gross) or 2,184 MW (exportable), the statement said.

"The combined cost estimate for project and the related liqueified natural gas receiving terminal are expected to make this the largest single foreign direct investment in India's energy sector," it said.
